Since
SINCE
prep. / adv.
Webster 1828 prints SINCE as preposition or adverb: after; from the time that. The proper signification is after, and its appropriate sense includes the whole period between an event and the present time. He cites Genesis 30:30 and the prophets who have been since the world began. Companion pages already treat world, time, and prophet.

Biblical Definition

Since in Scripture is not a filler and not a shrug. It is after — from the time that — the whole stretch between a named event and now, or the whole age from the world's beginning. Jacob says the LORD has blessed you since my coming (Genesis 30:30). Luke says He spoke by the mouth of His holy prophets, who have been since the world began (Luke 1:70). The man born blind says, Since the world began it has been unheard of that anyone opened the eyes of one who was born blind (John 9:32). The dictionary therefore keeps since from becoming a throat-clearing. It marks time after a named act of God.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828: SINCE, preposition or adverb — after; from the time that. The Lord hath blessed thee, since my coming (Genesis 30:30). Holy prophets, who have been since the world began. Also: ago; past. Also: because that.

expand to see more

SINCE, preposition or adverb

1. After; from the time that. The proper signification of since is after, and its appropriate sense includes the whole period between an event and the present time. I have not seen my brother since January. The Lord hath blessed thee, since my coming. Genesis 30:30. Holy prophets, who have been since the world began. Since then denotes, during the whole time after an event; or at any particular time during that period.

2. Ago; past; before this. About two years since an event happened, that is, two years having passed.

3. Because that; this being the fact that.

When it precedes a noun, it is called a preposition; when it precedes a sentence it is called an adverb. Webster ranks it with the prepositions.

Key Scripture

Genesis 30:30 — "For what you had before I came was little, and it has increased to a great amount; the LORD has blessed you since my coming. And now, when shall I also provide for my own house?”"

Luke 1:70 — "As He spoke by the mouth of His holy prophets, Who have been since the world began,"

John 9:32 — "Since the world began it has been unheard of that anyone opened the eyes of one who was born blind."

Modern Corruption

Since is corrupted when from-the-time-that is recast as a filler, when since-the-world-began is sold as ancient-history dismissal, and when the LORD's blessing since a named coming is dropped for luck.

expand to see more

The first corruption is since as throat-clearing. Webster's first sense is after; from the time that — the whole period between an event and now. A sentence that starts with since and never names the event is not that word.

The second corruption is the world's beginning as folklore. Luke 1:70 is holy prophets who have been since the world began. John 9:32 uses the same span to name an unheard-of mercy. Scoffing at the span is not scholarship.

The third corruption is blessing without a timestamp. Genesis 30:30 is the LORD has blessed you since my coming. The age keeps the increase and drops the since.
